clue.text: Dodgy surgeon accepts cape — it's what cadgers do

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes the next piece inside itself, as a host accepts a guest
something dodgy is unreliable or bent out of shape, so the letters of surgeon are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A shady surgeon takes a cape, which is just what spongers do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' reshuffles SURGEON to SROUNGE, and 'accepts' puts C inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadgers beg or sponge things from others, which is exactly what scrounging means.

clue.text: Jam initially provided for female in retreat

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, swapping the female letter out of the retreat word

parts.note: a flight is a hasty retreat from danger

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word provided is wanted

explanation.surface: A woman on the run is supplied with jam at the start of her escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P from 'provided', which replaces the F of FLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is a predicament or tight spot, the same idea as a sorry plight.

clue.text: Radio drama revealing exploit in scrubby ground?

indicators.note: the exploiting word is placed inside the word for scrubby ground

parts.note: underwood is low scrub or undergrowth beneath trees
to milk something is to exploit it for all it is worth

explanation.surface: A radio play shows somebody taking advantage of rough, scrubby land.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas's famous play for voices was written for radio, so the definition is exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas's piece about a Welsh village was written as a play for voices on radio.

clue.text: Iron ring circled by small insect

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

indicators.note: the ring letter is surrounded by the insect word, placed within it

parts.note: a moth is a winged insect
O is a ring from its round shape

explanation.surface: A little bug flies around a metal ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circled by' puts O inside MOTH to give MOOTH, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press out creases and make them flat and even.

clue.text: One who conspired with Scottish fellow, showing spice

parts.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators against Julius Caesar
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A plotter who worked alongside a Scot turns out to be selling spice.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant bark from a tropical tree is one of the most common kitchen spices.

clue.text: Nice dances disposed to make us glow

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Dances in Nice are set up to make everybody radiant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city; it is merely letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To incandesce is to become white-hot and give off light, so to glow.

clue.text: Sudden wind evident in last two-thirds of month

indicators.note: only the final two thirds of the month's name survive, the first third being dropped

parts.note: August is the eighth month

explanation.surface: A sudden breeze shows up in late summer.
explanation.walkthrough: AUGUST has six letters; dropping the first two leaves the final four.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief sudden rush of wind is called a blast or flurry of air.

clue.text: Sparkling drink son dipped into an hour after midday

indicators.note: the son letter is plunged inside the time phrase

parts.note: one o'clock in the afternoon is at one, written AT I with I for one

explanation.surface: A boy goes for a fizzy drink at one in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: One hour after midday is one o'clock, 'at one', with the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian sparkling white wine comes from Piedmont and is named after its home town.

clue.text: Animal father's taken round hospital — husky, say?

indicators.note: the father word is wrapped around the hospital letter

parts.note: a sire is a father, used especially of animals
H is the abbreviation for hospital, on road signs

indicators.note: say signals a word heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a husky voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: Dad has carried a sled dog to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' tempts as the dog and the answer, but it means hoarse, which sounds like the second word. A Shire horse is a big English draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of heavy English draught horse is a large farm animal.

clue.text: Immediately cause irreparable damage to broadcast on radio

indicators.note: a radio listener hears words without seeing how they are spelt

parts.note: to write off a car is to damage it beyond repair

explanation.surface: Something smashed beyond repair goes straight out on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something straight away, without delay, is doing it at once.

clue.text: Unidentified person the writer's girl recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's is my
Nona is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone nameless remembers the author's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: MY NONA read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is someone whose name is unknown or concealed, a nameless individual.

clue.text: A jolly smooth article originally marking a new play

parts.note: Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM
to sand wood is to smooth it
the is the definite article

indicators.note: the first letter of marking is taken

explanation.surface: Someone lays out an essay smoothly, writing a new drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' and 'smooth' look like describing words, but they are a marine and a verb. Shaw's comedy takes its title from Virgil.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote this comedy about war and romance in 1894.

clue.text: Idiomatic expression gets worn at the edges, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is spoken, not written

parts.note: cloth that frays gets worn and ragged at the edges

explanation.surface: An expression becomes threadbare, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic expression is a fixed group of words, a set form of words.

clue.text: Classical scholar the French can introduce is German

indicators.note: the first two pieces come before the last one, introducing it

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a tin is a can
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: A French tin presented by a German academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies Latin language and literature is a classical scholar.

clue.text: Frequenter of St James's perhaps — one in suit on island?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a club is one card of the suit of clubs
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man in a suit on an island hangs about a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: St James's is an area of London famous for its gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who frequents gentlemen's clubs, as in St James's in London, is a regular club member.

clue.text: Like fusspot's long-standing desire to tour sultanate

definitions.note: 's stands for is, so the definition is like a fusspot

parts.note: something long-standing is old

indicators.note: the desire word goes round the sultanate, encircling it

parts.note: a wish is a desire
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A fussy person has an old dream of a trip to Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' signals that one piece goes round the other; 'fusspot's' carries 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fussy, timid and prim behaviour is typically and unkindly described this way.

clue.text: Old PM's right to appear in traditional drama

indicators.note: the right abbreviation shows up inside the drama word

parts.note: Noh is traditional Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is entitled to perform in a classic play.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782.

clue.text: Fellow briefly appearing in French art displays

indicators.note: the fellow's name shows up inside the French word

parts.note: thou art is tu es in French
Vince is a man's name, short for Vincent

explanation.surface: A man shows up briefly in French art exhibitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb of 'thou art', so French ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a quality is to show or reveal it clearly.

clue.text: Dog training family say raised north of the Home Counties

indicators.note: in a down clue everything before sits above the last piece

parts.note: PE is physical education or training
kin is family

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: Training a family dog, say, up north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the example word upwards. The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: This small long-haired toy breed originated in China.

clue.text: W African language also used in Djibouti?

indicators.note: the letters are found within the place name

explanation.surface: A West African tongue is also spoken in the Horn of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This language of south-east Nigeria is more often spelt Igbo.

clue.text: Unsightly building mostly accommodating fish

indicators.note: the shortened building holds the fish inside it
most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: a house is a building
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An ugly building mostly houses fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the building, and 'accommodating' puts the fish inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hideous is extremely ugly or repulsive to look at.

clue.text: Like conquerors a long complex opera originally named?

indicators.note: complex means intricate or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini

indicators.note: the first letter of named is wanted

explanation.surface: Something long and elaborate, like an opera, is first given a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges A LONG to ANGLO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans who conquered England in 1066 became the Anglo-Norman ruling class.

clue.text: Put out, seeing investigator's place

parts.note: a DI, detective inspector, is an investigator
to place something is to locate it

explanation.surface: A detective visits the scene, putting him off.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a shoulder is to wrench it out of its joint.

clue.text: Roll an honoured companion leaves on plate?

parts.note: to roll is to spin or turn over
an is the indefinite article A
CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: A distinguished companion departs from a bread roll on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departing; it is the vegetable's edible leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This green vegetable is eaten as leaves, served on a dinner plate.

clue.text: One doesn't believe daughter brought up in part of square

indicators.note: in a down clue the daughter letter is moved higher in the word

parts.note: the infield is the central area of a cricket field around the square

explanation.surface: A girl is raised on part of a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' moves the D of INFIELD above the E and L. The cricket square is the pitch area in the infield.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is a person who does not hold a religious faith.

clue.text: In Scotland one hangs loosely around saws

indicators.note: the hanging word is placed around the Scots one

parts.note: something that sags droops or hangs loosely
yin is Scots for one

explanation.surface: In Scotland a man hangs loosely around some tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saws' looks like tools; it means old proverbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Old saws are proverbs or maxims, wise traditional sayings.

clue.text: Former tennis star beginning to tackle substantial dish

parts.note: Arthur Ashe was a Wimbledon champion

indicators.note: the first letter of tackle is taken

explanation.surface: A tennis great starts to tuck into a hearty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Scottish and northern English word for a large serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashet is a large plate or serving platter for meat, in Scots usage.

clue.text: Bird that died out in Missouri area

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: An extinct bird is found in a region of Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird, extinct for centuries.
